/Users/myguyfriday/.openclaw/workspace/mission-control/sermon-dev/Sermons/defined-who-god-says-you-are/Week-4-God-Says-I-Am-More-Than-a-Conqueror/Week-4_Manuscript.html

**Sermon Title:** "God Says I Am More Than a Conqueror"
**Date:** May 3, 2026
**Passage:** Romans 8:28-39
**Runtime:** 35-40 minutes

Write the manuscript using this exact structure:

**INTRODUCTION** (~5-6 min): 
Hook: "There's a word the world uses a lot — hyper-nikomen — 'more than conquerors.' MostChristians have never heard it unpacked this way. Most people think identity is declared. But Paul describes something being PRODUCED in you. The question: Is that identity actually being produced in your life?"
[Then transition to Romans 8:28-39 — Paul's triumphant chapter]

**POINT 1: YOU BECOME THE VICTOR** (~5-6 min)
Romans 8:28 — "We know that in all things God works for good."
Key line: "God doesn't promise to give you a good story. He promises to write a good ending into yours."
Illustrate with: The Post-it Note story — Spencer Silver's "failed" adhesive became 3M's most profitable product.
Application: When difficulty hits, say "God is working this for my good" instead of "How do I fix this?"

**POINT 2: YOU BECOME A WORSHIPPER** (~5-6 min)
Romans 8:31-32 — God gave His Son. Will He not also freely give us all things?
Key line: "The God who didn't spare His own Son will not hold back anything else either."
Illustrate with: Rites of passage research — rituals don't just symbolize identity change, they PRODUCE it.
Application: Stop asking "Did I go to church?" Ask "Did I worship?" Treat driving, working, parenting as worship.

**POINT 3: YOU BECOME ABLE** (~5-6 min)
Romans 8:34 — Christ is at the right hand of God interceding for us.
Key line: "You're not fighting alone. The one who defeated death is speaking up for you."
Illustrate with: John Wimber — "I have no confidence in my abilities. I have total confidence in the Holy Spirit."
Application: When overwhelmed, stop and pray "I am not enough. I need You" before anything else.

**POINT 4: YOU BECOME COURAGEOUS** (~5-6 min)
Romans 8:37 — "More than conquerors" (hyper-nikomen)
Key line: "You don't just survive hard times. You come out of them with more of Christ than you went in with."
Illustrate with: The sold-out concert ticket — you walk in without anxiety because your ticket is already punched. Courage isn't manufactured. It's the overflow of knowing you're already in.
Application: When fear shows up, ask "Am I trusting the One who already won?" not "Do I have enough courage?"

**POINT 5: YOU BECOME SECURE** (~5-6 min)
Romans 8:38-39 + Philippians 3:20 — Nothing separates us from God's love. Our citizenship is in heaven.
Key line: "The question isn't whether God's love is big enough. The question is whether you believe you're already home."
Illustrate with: Anchor and the storm — the anchor doesn't stop the storm. It keeps the ship from drifting. When everything else moves, you want to be anchored to something that doesn't.
Application: Write "Citizen of Heaven" somewhere you'll see it daily.

**CONCLUSION + CALL** (~4-5 min):
Maslow pyramid gap: Psychology describes the need for unconditional acceptance but can't supply it. That's the gap only the gospel fills.

Call to action: "If you've been working to earn God's love — stop. Receive it. It's yours. Not because you performed. Because He gave it to you before you were born. Stop performing. Start receiving."

Decision moment: Baptisms / Rededication

---

IMPORTANT: Write this as a FULL MANUSCRIPT — complete sentences written out for speaking, not bullet points. Make it flow like someone is actually preaching it. Save the HTML file to the exact path above. The file must be created.
I have the outline and the Week 1 style. Writing the full manuscript now.

God Says I Am His Child

18
19 Series: Defined — Who God Says You Are | Week 1 | April 12, 2026
20 Romans 8:1–17 | ReImage Church — Pastor Chris 21
22

Have you ever had someone try to give you something — a real gift, no strings — and you just couldn't take it?

23

Like, somebody at a restaurant says, "Hey, I got your meal." And before they even finish the sentence, you're reaching for your wallet. "No, no, no — let me at least get the tip." And they're like, "I said I got it." And you're like, "You sure? I can Venmo you." They are literally handing you a gift and you are negotiating your way into paying for it.

24

Come on. We all do this.

25

And here's the thing — we don't just do it at restaurants. We do it with God.

26

God says, "You're mine. You're in. You're my child." And we say, "Okay, but let me earn it first. Let me prove I'm worth it. Let me pray enough and read my Bible enough and serve enough and be good enough — and then maybe I'll believe it."

27

I want to be honest with you this morning. I've been a Christian for a long time. My dad was a pastor. I grew up in the church. I've been in ministry for decades. And there are still weeks — real weeks, recent weeks — where I wake up and the first thought in my head is, "Is God pleased with me today?" And that question sits on my chest like a weight. I know better. I know the theology. I can teach it. I've preached it to you. But knowing it and living in it are two different things.

28

How many of you have had that thought? Come on, don't be shy. I've had it this week.

29

That voice — the one that says you have to keep earning it, keep proving it, keep performing — that's what I call the orphan voice. And if you've heard it, this message is for you.

30

Because here's what God wants you to know today. You're not an orphan trying to earn a home. You're a child who's already home.

31

This is Week 1 of a new series called "Defined" — four weeks about who God says you are. Not who you think you are. Not who the world says you are. Who God says you are. And it starts here: you are His child.

32

Let me pray for us, and then we'll get into the text.

33

Father, we thank you that you've called us your children. Open our eyes to see who you say we are. Remove the lies we've believed about ourselves and replace them with your truth. We want to hear from you today. In Jesus' name, amen.

34

[FULL READING OF ROMANS 8:1–17 — INSERT HERE]

35

All right. I want to start with something that changed everything for me when I finally understood it. Because for a long time, I had the gospel partly right and partly sideways. And the part I had sideways was costing me more than I realized.

36

For years I thought forgiveness was the headline. The main event. I thought the gospel was basically: God forgives your sins, and if you hold it together, you get to go to heaven. And that is true — but it's not the whole truth. It's not even the best part.

37

Because here's what happens when forgiveness is your primary understanding of the Christian life. You wake up every day trying not to sin. You try to pray enough. You try to read your Bible enough. ...

101
1. Each time a difficult situation arises this week, say out loud: "God is working this for my good."
102
2. Identify one circumstance you've been complaining about and write down how God might use it.
103
3. Stop one negative thought about your situation and replace it with the truth of Romans 8:28.
104 105 106 107
108

POINT 2: YOU BECOME A WORSHIPPER

110

Romans 8:31-32 — "He who did not spare His own Son, but delivered Him up for us all — how shall He not with Him also freely give us all things?"

111

Identity Marker: You are not a Sunday singer — you are a 7-day-a-week worshiper.

112
113 114

The Truth

115

When you truly believe God gave His Son for you, worship stops being a Sunday performance and starts being a lifestyle. Your whole life becomes the song.

116 117

Observation

118

Worship has become an event instead of a posture. People check the box on Sunday and call it done — when the New Testament call is to offer your whole life as worship (Romans 12:1).

119 120

Application

121

Stop asking "Did I go to church?" and start asking "Did I worship?" Treat everything as worship — how you drive, how you speak to your kids, how you handle the difficult client.

122 123
124 Quotable Line: "The God who didn't spare His own Son will not hold back anything else either." 125
126 127
128

💡 Illustration — Rites of Passage (Sociology/Anthropology)

129

Sociologists have studied how rituals actually transform identity. In cultures around the world, coming-of-age rituals don't just symbolize a transition — they produce it. The ritual creates the new identity.

130

Christians have forgotten this. We treat worship as a symbol of faith rather than a mechanism of transformation. But when the author of Hebrews tells us to "consider how to stir up one another to love and good works" (Heb 10:24), he's pointing to a mechanism — gathering produces the gathering identity.

131

Connection: Every time you show up, every time you offer your Monday as worship, you're not just expressing who you are — you're forming who you are.

132
133 134

Next Step Actions

135
1. Each morning this week, before checking your phone, say: "Lord, today is Yours — I'm worshipping You in how I work, speak, and love."
136
2. Choose one mundane task (driving, cooking, doing dishes) and intentionally do it as an act of worship this week.
137
3. This Sunday, after the service ends, ask one person: "How was your worship this week?" — and share how you worshipped in an ordinary moment.

145

146
147 148

The Truth

149

When you know Christ is actively interceding for you at this very moment, weakness stops being a liability. You're not capable in yourself — you're enabled by grace.
